meta.aciklama:
Comment "AUTHOR" and I'll DM you the link to the one Claude Code setting that takes Claude's name off your commits (or signs them your way). Follow so the DM lands 📩

👇 READ BELOW for what's inside:

1. By default, every commit Claude Code makes for you ends with a Co-Authored-By line naming the model, and every pull request it opens ends with "Generated with Claude Code".

2. Add "attribution": false to ~/.claude/settings.json and it strips all of it: commits, pull requests and the session link.

3. Or set "commit" and "pr" to your own text, so every commit is signed your way. Put it in .claude/settings.json to set it for your whole team.

4. Don't want to touch the file? The DM has one prompt you paste into Claude and it makes the change for you.

The catch: "attribution": false needs Claude Code v2.1.281 or newer (older versions skip the whole file), and some teams and open-source projects ask you to show when AI helped. Check their rules first.

For the link, comment "AUTHOR"

#claudeai #claudecode #claude #claudetips

transkript.t: Everyone building with Claude is letting Claude take credit for your work on every commit,
because by default, each commit gets a co-authored byline with the model's name,
and every pull request it opens even gets a robot tag.
But one line in your settings, attribution false, strips it all off.
Then, you can even sign every commit your own way,
and you never open the file, because one prompt makes Claude do it.
